thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: GPU pool saturation (us-west-2) — queue depth > 200, latency SLO breaches. Auto-escalate to #eng-oncall.
akash: I'm on it, grabbing logs and current HPA state.
sara: Thanks. Any customer-facing impact?
akash: Early signal from metrics: 12 customers with >95th percentile requests failing to get a slot within 2s. Notified CS to flag top 3.
mike: Repro tip: this looks like the cold-start/warmup lag we saw last week when queue spikes coincide with pod churn.
lee: Can you paste HPA and pool occupancy?
akash: k8s HPA and pool snapshot:```
HPA mymodel-scaler: currentReplicas=8, desiredReplicas=8, targetCPUUtilizationPercentage=70
GPU-Pool(us-west-2): total_gpus=64, allocated_gpus=64, queued_jobs=218, warmup_in_progress=6
Deployment hotpool: pending_pods=4, pod_status=[ContainerCreating x4]
```
jen: Warmup tasks show stuck image pull on 4 new nodes (registry throttling). Logs:```
Pulling image "redwood/runtime:optimized-v2"
error: net/http: TLS handshake timeout
```
akash: Hypothesis 1: registry throttling + image size => slow warmup => HPA can't enlarge effective capacity fast enough. Hypothesis 2: autoscaler config not accounting for GPU warmup lead time.
sara: Mitigations? Fast options first.
mike: 1) Roll fallback to quantized smaller image (redwood/runtime:optimized-v2-q4) to reduce pull time and RAM. 2) Temporarily bump desiredReplicas to 12 to force allocation (if cluster has headroom). 3) Route low-priority customers to CPU-mode pool.
lee: Check cluster headroom:```
Cluster nodes: 8 nodes with available allocatable GPUs: 0
Node autoscaler: scaling disabled due to quota in zone a
```
akash: Not enough immediate headroom. Node autoscaler blocked. Requesting quota bump is slow.
jen: Can we enable image prefetch on nodes that still have spare NIC bandwidth? ops-runbook-bot: runbook step 3: `prefetch_image registry redwood/runtime:optimized-v2-q4 --nodes=all` (requires infra perms).
sara: Do we have infra perms in-call? @mike can you run the prefetch?
mike: Running prefetch now. Started on 12 nodes. Progress: 3/12 done.
akash: Meanwhile enabling fallback routing: applied config to route customers tagged `non-critical` -> cpu-fallback pool. Command: `redwoodctl route update --selector non-critical --pool cpu-fallback`
jen: CS update: 3 customers marked critical (enterprise), they're seeing degraded latency but no 5xx. Others see 502s.
lee: Any way to short-circuit warmup? Maybe start warmup containers with a minimal image then replace. Risky but could reduce start time.
mike: Idea: scale a small number of pre-warmed pods from the quantized image into the GPU pool by creating a DaemonSet that schedules lightweight warmup pods on nodes — quick to pull. If prefetch completes we should be fine. Kicking that off.
akash: New logs show container creation succeeded on 6 nodes after prefetch finished. queued_jobs drops from 218 -> 142.
sara: Good. Keep an eye on 95th latency. Can we compute timeline for RCA? We need to collect: HPA events, cluster autoscaler events, image pull errors, queue depth timeline, APM traces for affected requests.
jen: Pulling APM slice for affected customers now. ETA ~8m.
lee: I'll capture cluster-autoscaler logs and the registry error traces. Pasting recent errors:```
2026-03-17T12:03:21Z registry: request throttled: 429 Too Many Requests
2026-03-17T12:03:22Z kubelet: failed to pull image: net/http: TLS handshake timeout
2026-03-17T12:04:05Z autoscaler: scale_up blocked - quota limit reached in zone a
```
akash: Noted. Recording hypotheses in thread: - H1: image pull throttling caused warmup delay -> queue buildup. - H2: HPA configured solely on CPU -> doesn't pre-scale for GPU warmup lag. - H3: Node autoscaler quota prevented fast scale-up.
mike: Mitigation status: prefetch complete 12/12, started 8 quantized warm pods, routed non-critical traffic to cpu-fallback, increased desiredReplicas for 10 minutes to force extra pods where possible. Queued jobs now 60.
sara: Good. Do we need a handoff? I'm going to sleep in 30m; if this continues past that please escalate to oncall+infra.
jen: APM shows tail latency spike aligns with warmup gap 12:02–12:10 UTC. No evidence of code-level regressions.
lee: Captured and archived cluster logs to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2955554321/cluster-logs.tar.gz
akash: Creating timeline snippet for RCA:```
12:01: alert triggered - queue > 200
12:02: image pull throttling starts (429)
12:03: hpa remains at 8; autoscaler blocked by quota
12:05: prefetch started
12:07: first warm pods available -> queued drops to 140
12:12: fallback routing applied -> queued drops to 60
12:18: latency begins returning toward SLO
```
sara: Nice. Action items: (1) infra to request registry egress/throughput increase and assess registry throttling (owners: infra) (2) runtime to add HPA tie-breaker metric for queue depth or warmup-probing (owners: eng-runtime) (3) ops to validate node autoscaler quotas in us-west-2 (owners: eng-infra) (4) postmortem draft with timeline + customer impact (owners: oncall).
mike: I'll file the postmortem seed and attach logs. jen: filing CS outreach for the 3 critical customers.
ops-runbook-bot: Handoff checklist: `incident_state=mitigated`, `followup=true`, assign owners: infra, eng-runtime, eng-infra, oncall`.
sara: Handing off to followups. If anything spikes, ping @oncall. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
